draft.title: The Anzac legend
card: The Anzac legend is a story told about Australian soldiers of World War I. It praises courage, mateship and endurance in hard conditions.
It grew from the Gallipoli landing and wartime writing, and Anzac Day on 25 April is used to remember it.
Historians debate how well the legend fits what soldiers lived through. Some soldiers also felt fear, boredom or anger, and not all of them behaved like the heroes in the story.
Historians also ask whose stories it leaves out. Women, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander soldiers and others are often missing from the picture.
draft.remember: The Anzac legend praises courage and mateship, but historians question how true it is to soldiers' lives and who it leaves out.

a.q: Which pair of qualities does the Anzac legend praise most?
a.why: The legend honours courage and mateship, meaning loyalty to your mates. The other pairs are not the qualities it is known for.
a.clue: Think of what is said about soldiers helping each other.

b.q: A historian says the Anzac legend leaves out the stories of Aboriginal soldiers. What kind of debate is she raising?
opts: Whose experiences the legend leaves out
Whether the landing happened on 25 April
Whether soldiers were paid for service
b.why: She is asking whose stories are missing from the legend. The date of the landing is not in dispute.
b.clue: Look at the word leaves out.

b.best: Whose experiences the legend leaves out

proposal.remember: The Anzac legend praises courage and mateship, but historians question how true it is to soldiers' lives and who it leaves out.

a.q: Which pair of qualities does the Anzac legend praise most?
a.why: The legend honours courage and mateship, meaning loyalty to your mates, along with endurance. Obedience and discipline may sound like soldierly qualities, but they are not what the legend is known for.
a.clue: Think of what the story says about soldiers sticking by each other.

b.q: A historian reads letters from Australian soldiers in France. Many describe fear, boredom and anger at their officers. Which debate about the Anzac legend does this evidence add to?
opts: How well it matches what soldiers lived through
Whose wartime stories it does not include
Why it grew from the Gallipoli landing
Why Anzac Day is held on 25 April
b.why: The letters show soldiers' real feelings, which do not always fit the heroic story, so they test how well the legend matches soldiers' lives. They are not about people missing from the legend, because these soldiers are the ones it already describes.
b.clue: Are these soldiers missing from the story, or shown differently from it?
